title: Test Normal Cases
outcome: By the end, I can test routine cases against expectations and count full passes honestly.
scenario: A fictional pencil-pouch finder has been run on four ordinary requests.
given: Catalogue: P1 capacity 3, P2 capacity 7; first fitting pouch. Valid whole counts 1–9.
Requests 2,4,6,8; recorded outputs P1,P2,P1,none. These are invented records, not class results.

steps.label: Compare outputs
steps.detail: Runs at 2,4 and 8 agree; run at 6 disagrees.

steps.label: Trace failure
steps.detail: P1 holds only 3, so it cannot satisfy request 6.

steps.label: Report
steps.detail: Three of four routine cases pass; retain the failure.

explanation: An ordinary case is not automatically correct. Define expected outputs from the contract before reading prototype outputs. Checking both selected ID and eligibility catches the wrong P1 suggestion. A no-match output can be a full pass when that is exactly what the valid request requires.

counterfactual.change: Prototype reports none for request 6 instead of P1.
counterfactual.reason: P2 can hold 6, so none is also wrong under the first-fit rule.

student_task: Why is none correct for 8 but incorrect for 6? Use both capacity cards.
teacher_answer: Neither capacity 3 nor 7 reaches 8. Capacity 7 does reach 6, so P2 is required for 6.
project_evidence: Maintain sorter tests with input, independently derived expectation, actual output, version and full-pass judgment.
limits: Four routine tests do not cover equality, invalid inputs or every relevant classroom condition.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.
